# Cavan's Website

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Site build](https://github.com/cavandonohoe/cavandonohoe.github.io/actions/workflows/pages-rmarkdown.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/cavandonohoe/cavandonohoe.github.io/actions/workflows/pages-rmarkdown.yml)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of my website is to display some fun side projects I have been working on. Movie data intrigues me, so I scraped IMDb to use some of their clean data. I also have my résumé here since it's easier to share a link than an attachment.

Check out my website at [https://cavandonohoe.github.io](https://cavandonohoe.github.io)

## Automation

The repo runs the following on a schedule via GitHub Actions. Anything
manual is a click away on the Actions tab.

### Site build & previews

* `pages-branch-previews.yml` -- main deploy + per-PR preview deploy
  and cleanup. This is what publishes the site (pushes to the
  `gh-pages` branch).
* `pages-rmarkdown.yml` -- daily safety-net build with DESCRIPTION /
  `library()` validation and gs4 guard checks. Does **not** deploy
  (deploy is owned by `pages-branch-previews.yml` to avoid Pages
  deployment races).
* `quick-rating-plot.yml` -- when a PR adds a show to
  `scripts/shows_manifest.R`, fetches its IMDb ratings, commits the CSV
  to the PR, and comments the heatmap PNG inline (hosted on the
  `quick-plots` branch) a few minutes before the full preview lands.

### Scheduled refreshes (commit to `main`)

* `update_imdb_ratings.yml` -- weekly IMDb episode ratings refresh.
* `update_top1000_box_office.yml` -- monthly Best Picture + Top 1000
  box office refresh.
* `update_top250_with_rt.yml` -- monthly Top 250 + Rotten Tomatoes
  refresh.
* `update_director_filmographies.yml` -- monthly TMDb director
  filmography refresh for the Director Box Office Trajectory page.
* `update_sp500.yml` -- weekly VOO price refresh.
* `update_us_rentals.yml` -- monthly Zillow ZHVI/ZORI refresh.
* `update_mymaps_export.yml` -- weekly Google My Maps export.
* `update_watched_episodes.yml` -- weekly episode list for every rated
  series in my IMDb export.
* `update_imdb_exceptional_episodes.yml` -- weekly Exceptional IMDb
  Episodes refresh.
* `update_confederate_statues_data.yml` -- monthly Confederate statues
  data refresh.
* `update_movie_ranker_personal.yml` -- every 6 hours, pulls my personal
  Elo ratings from the movie-ranker Supabase project for My IMDb Ratings.
* `update_saved_episodes.yml` -- daily Spotify saved-episodes refresh,
  then redeploys the podcast dashboard on shinyapps.io.
* `update_tohs_reunion.yml` -- hourly TOHS reunion sheet snapshot.
* `update_page_views.yml` -- daily GA4 pull that reorders the homepage
  Projects grid by traffic.
* `shiny-traffic.yml` -- weekly snapshot of shinyapps.io traffic for
  every app on the account.
* `year-in-review.yml` -- daily current-year developer review, plus a
  Jan 1 snapshot of the year that just ended.
* `activity-art.yml` -- daily 30-day commit activity SVG.
* `lately.yml` -- daily summary of the last 30 days of my commits
  (`data/lately.json`).
* `personal-changelog.yml` -- daily changelog of PRs merged in the last
  30 days (`data/changelog.json`).
* `weekly-wrapped.yml` -- weekly 7-day activity snapshot
  (`data/weekly/`).
* `project-case-studies.yml` -- on push, rebuilds project case-study
  metadata (`data/project_case_studies.json`).
* `refresh-commit-activity.yml` -- weekly re-knit of this README's
  commit-activity charts.

The uniform ones (`update_sp500`, `update_us_rentals`,
`update_top250_with_rt`, `update_watched_episodes`) are thin callers of
`refresh-data.yml`, which owns the shared run/guard/commit/redeploy
logic. The rest stay standalone because they build dynamic commit
messages or need extra fetch steps. Every refresh that commits to `main`
runs `scripts/data_sanity.R` first, so an empty or collapsed scrape
fails the run instead of landing on `main`.

### Data refreshes (open PR)

* `update_best_picture_winners.yml` -- annual Oscar refresh.
* `rebuild_cv.yml` -- weekly CV PDF/DOCX rebuild from Google Sheet,
  opens a PR if anything changed.
* `refresh-sitemap.yml` -- weekly `sitemap.xml` regeneration.

### Site health

* `link-check.yml` -- weekly + on-PR broken-link check (lychee).
* `pa11y.yml` -- weekly accessibility audit (pa11y-ci).
* `lighthouse.yml` -- two modes: on-PR audit of the deployed preview URL
  with a score comment, plus a post-build audit of the production
  artifact after each successful main build.
* `repo-size.yml` -- weekly + on-PR repo-size report.
* `scheduled-failure-alert.yml` -- opens an issue when a scheduled
  workflow fails and closes it on the next green run.

### Code quality

* `lint.yml` -- on-PR lintr scan of changed R/Rmd files.
* `typos.yml` -- on-PR spell check.
* `pr-smoke.yml` -- on-PR fast render of only the changed Rmds.
* `test.yml` -- R test suite (`scripts/run_tests.R`) on PRs and pushes.

### Side apps

* `movie-ranker-build.yml` -- on-PR build of the Next.js movie-ranker
  app.
* `backfill-movie-ranker-posters.yml` -- weekly TMDB poster backfill
  for new movie-ranker titles.
* `ping-movie-ranker-supabase.yml` -- weekly read query so the
  free-tier Supabase project never auto-pauses.
* `tohs-apps-script.yml` -- validates and deploys the TOHS reunion
  Google Apps Script.

### Repo hygiene

* `.github/dependabot.yml` -- weekly bump of pinned GitHub Actions.
* `dependabot-automerge.yml` -- squash-merges minor/patch Dependabot
  PRs once all other checks pass.
* `labeler.yml` -- auto-label PRs by changed paths.
* `prune-previews.yml` -- weekly cleanup of stale PR preview deploys.
* `data-question.yml` -- acknowledges issues labeled `data-question`.

## Activity over time

The chart below summarizes commit activity on this repo: monthly
commit count and lines changed (insertions + deletions), split by
my own commits vs. automated commits from the scheduled data
refresh workflows above. Regenerated each time `README.Rmd` is
knit.

```{r commit-activity, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 8, fig.path = "images/readme/", dev = "png", dpi = 110, fig.alt = "Two bar charts showing monthly commits and monthly lines changed (insertions + deletions) for this repository, split by Cavan's own commits vs. scheduled-bot commits."}
# Bind the magrittr pipe locally so this chunk (and the cumulative/summary
# chunks that share the knit environment) render standalone without a prior
# library(dplyr) attach.
`%>%` <- magrittr::`%>%`

raw <- system(
  "git log --no-merges --pretty=format:'COMMIT|%H|%at|%an' --shortstat",
  intern = TRUE
)

commits <- list()
current <- NULL
for (line in raw) {
  if (startsWith(line, "COMMIT|")) {
    if (!is.null(current)) commits[[length(commits) + 1L]] <- current
    parts <- strsplit(line, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    current <- list(
      sha = parts[2L],
      ts = as.numeric(parts[3L]),
      author = parts[4L],
      ins = 0L,
      del = 0L
    )
  } else if (nchar(line) > 0 && !is.null(current)) {
    ins_m <- regmatches(line, regexpr("([0-9]+) insertion", line))
    del_m <- regmatches(line, regexpr("([0-9]+) deletion", line))
    if (length(ins_m)) current$ins <- as.integer(sub(" insertion.*", "", ins_m))
    if (length(del_m)) current$del <- as.integer(sub(" deletion.*", "", del_m))
  }
}
if (!is.null(current)) commits[[length(commits) + 1L]] <- current

df <- dplyr::bind_rows(commits) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as.POSIXct(ts, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
    month = lubridate::floor_date(as.Date(date), "month"),
    # All non-bot commits are mine; STEPHANIE HUSSEY is just me on her laptop.
    is_bot = grepl("\\[bot\\]|github-actions", author, ignore.case = TRUE),
    author_type = factor(
      ifelse(is_bot, "Automated (bots)", "Cavan"),
      levels = c("Cavan", "Automated (bots)")
    ),
    lines_changed = ins + del
  )

month_seq <- seq(min(df$month), max(df$month), by = "month")
monthly <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  month = month_seq,
  author_type = levels(df$author_type)
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(month, author_type) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(
        commits = dplyr::n(),
        lines_changed = sum(lines_changed),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = c("month", "author_type")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::replace_na(list(commits = 0L, lines_changed = 0L)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    author_type = factor(author_type, levels = c("Cavan", "Automated (bots)"))
  )

palette <- c("Cavan" = "#2c7fb8", "Automated (bots)" = "#f0a202")

theme_readme <- ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)
  )

p_commits <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  monthly,
  ggplot2::aes(x = month, y = commits, fill = author_type)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 25) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = palette, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Commits per month",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Commits"
  ) +
  theme_readme

p_lines <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  monthly %>% dplyr::filter(lines_changed > 0),
  ggplot2::aes(x = month, y = lines_changed, fill = author_type)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge2(width = 25, preserve = "single"),
    width = 25
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = palette, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    limits = range(month_seq),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    trans = "log10",
    labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Lines changed per month (insertions + deletions, log scale)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Lines changed"
  ) +
  theme_readme

patchwork::wrap_plots(p_commits, p_lines, ncol = 1) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r commit-activity-cumulative, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 7, fig.path = "images/readme/", dev = "png", dpi = 110, fig.alt = "Two cumulative line charts showing total commits and total lines changed (insertions + deletions) over time, split by Cavan's own commits vs. scheduled-bot commits."}
cumulative <- monthly %>%
  dplyr::arrange(author_type, month) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(author_type) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cum_commits = cumsum(commits),
    cum_lines = cumsum(lines_changed)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

p_cum_commits <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  cumulative,
  ggplot2::aes(x = month, y = cum_commits, colour = author_type)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = palette, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Cumulative commits",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Cumulative commits"
  ) +
  theme_readme

p_cum_lines <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  cumulative,
  ggplot2::aes(x = month, y = cum_lines, colour = author_type)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = palette, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Cumulative lines changed (insertions + deletions)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Cumulative lines changed"
  ) +
  theme_readme

patchwork::wrap_plots(p_cum_commits, p_cum_lines, ncol = 1) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r commit-activity-summary, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, results = "asis"}
total_commits <- nrow(df)
total_lines <- sum(df$lines_changed)
total_cavan <- sum(df$author_type == "Cavan")
total_bots <- sum(df$author_type == "Automated (bots)")
first_commit <- min(df$date)
cat(sprintf(
  paste0(
    "*%s commits from %s to %s (%s by me, %s by scheduled bots), ",
    "touching %s lines in total.*\n"
  ),
  format(total_commits, big.mark = ","),
  format(first_commit, "%b %Y"),
  format(max(df$date), "%b %Y"),
  format(total_cavan, big.mark = ","),
  format(total_bots, big.mark = ","),
  format(total_lines, big.mark = ",")
))
```

## Setup and Local Development

Local development, prerequisites, build steps, lint/test commands, and PR conventions all live in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

### Quick IMDb Rating Plot

Preview a show's season x episode heatmap in seconds, using the same
fetch and plotting code as the
[IMDb Rating Plot](https://cavandonohoe.github.io/imdb_rating_plot.html)
page, instead of waiting on CI and the full site build:

```bash
Rscript scripts/quick_rating_plot.R tt2085059 "Black Mirror"
```

This writes `data/<slug>_ep_ratings.csv` and
`imdb_rating_plot_files/<title>.png`, then opens the PNG. Add `--pr` to
also register the show with the weekly scraper and the shows manifest,
commit on a new branch off `origin/main`, and open a PR that adds it to
the page.

Without a local R setup (e.g. from a phone or a cloud coding agent), open
a PR that only adds the show's row to `scripts/shows_manifest.R` and to
the scraper's show list. `quick-rating-plot.yml` fetches the data on
GitHub Actions and comments the plot on the PR.

### Chase Statement Parser

The Chase statement parser is a local utility for turning Chase credit
card statement PDFs into a transaction workbook. It is designed so the
repo can keep reusable code without committing private finance data.

Privacy rules:

- Do not commit statement PDFs, generated workbooks, exported
  transaction CSVs, or Google Sheet URLs.
- Keep personal owner rules in `config/chase_owner_rules.csv`; that
  file is ignored by git.
- Use `config/chase_owner_rules.example.csv` as the tracked starting
  rules file for non-sensitive patterns and labels.

Parse statements locally:

```bash
Rscript scripts/parse_chase_statements.R \
  --rules config/chase_owner_rules.csv \
  --out data/chase_tx.xlsx \
  statements/*.pdf
```

Upload an already-generated workbook to a Google Sheet:

```bash
Rscript scripts/upload_chase_tx_to_gsheet.R \
  data/chase_tx.xlsx \
  "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/YOUR_SHEET_ID/edit"
```

The R parser is the canonical workflow. The Python parser supports the
same rules CSV format, but the R path is what this repo validates with
synthetic tests.

Parsing real PDFs with the R script requires the optional `pdftools`
package and its system Poppler libraries. The synthetic tests do not
require PDF parsing dependencies.

Run the synthetic parser smoke test:

```bash
Rscript tests/test_chase_parser.R
```

### Project Structure

- `*.Rmd` files: Individual pages of the website
- `_site.yml`: Site configuration and navigation
- `_common.R`: Common R code (Google auth setup for CI)
- `header/header.html`: HTML header with meta tags and favicons
- `include_footer.html`: Footer with contact links
- `css/footer.css`: Footer styling
- `.github/workflows/`: GitHub Actions workflows for CI/CD
- `data/`: Data files used by various pages
- `scripts/`: Utility scripts (e.g., ensuring gs4 guards)
- `tests/`: R tests run by `test.yml`
- `podcast-dashboard/`, `movie-ranker/`, `detour-finder/`,
  `streaming-history/`: self-contained side apps
- `tools/tohs-apps-script/`: Google Apps Script for the TOHS reunion

### Deployment

The site is automatically deployed to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions when changes are pushed to the `main` branch. See the Automation section above for the full list of workflows.
